themes_detail.label: Garbage collection crisis escalating
themes_detail.summary: Missed Collection complaints surged to 6 THIS WEEK (compared to 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks), a 2300% spike with z-score of 13.28—the most statistically anomalous issue in the district. This aligns with long-standing community board requests for increased sanitation trucks, suggesting systemic capacity failure.
evidence: 6 Missed Collection complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 13.28)
Community Board has repeatedly requested 'new or increase number of sanitation trucks and other equipment' from DSNY—request appears year after year, unsolved
HEAT/HOT WATER remains dominant category (5131 complaints over 90 days), suggesting aging infrastructure may be compounding sanitation workforce strain
reporting_angles: Interview sanitation workers and residents in affected blocks; request DSNY data on crew availability and route changes THIS WEEK
Investigate whether the recent spike correlates with staffing shortages, equipment breakdown, or route consolidation

themes_detail.label: Residential disposal complaints jump
themes_detail.summary: Residential Disposal Complaints jumped to 6 THIS WEEK vs. 1.8 weekly average (243% spike, z-score: 5.13), indicating acute waste-management or tenant compliance issues appearing now.
evidence: 6 Residential Disposal Complaint 311 calls THIS WEEK vs. 1.8 weekly average (z-score: 5.13)
Spike is NEW and sharper than Missed Collection spike 2 weeks ago; suggests internal/building-level issue rather than city service failure
Overlaps with Unsanitary Condition (720 complaints over 90 days) and animal-related spikes, suggesting interconnected waste/hygiene problem
reporting_angles: Identify which buildings or blocks are generating these complaints; interview building managers and residents about recent changes in disposal rules or enforcement
Determine if spike is tied to new composting mandate, recycling enforcement, or rodent complaints

themes_detail.label: Unsanitary animal conditions spike
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary Animal Pvt Property complaints reached 5 LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (1233% spike, z-score: 9.55), the second-highest statistical anomaly, paired with Dead Animal complaints spiking to 3 two weeks ago vs. 0.1 average. This indicates an emerging rodent or pest crisis.
evidence: 5 Unsanitary Animal Pvt Property complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 9.55)
3 Dead Animal complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 8.69)
Community Board has consistently requested 'animal and pest control requests including reducing rat and mosquito populations' from DOHMH, unresolved year after year
reporting_angles: Investigate whether the missed garbage collection spike (THIS WEEK) is creating food sources for rats; interview DOHMH about rodent baiting and trap deployment in the district
Map the geographic cluster of dead animal and unsanitary condition complaints to identify hotspots and environmental conditions

themes_detail.label: Outdoor building violations escalate
themes_detail.summary: OUTSIDE BUILDING complaints surged to 6 LAST WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 7.94), suggesting a sharp increase in exterior code violations, structural damage, or illegal construction activity.
evidence: 6 OUTSIDE BUILDING complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 7.94)
371 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (328 alterations, 10 new buildings), indicating significant construction activity may be triggering violations
Hill Top Apartments (1727 Amsterdam Ave) ULURP application is in Public Review, potentially creating adjacent construction disturbance
reporting_angles: Cross-reference the 6 OUTSIDE BUILDING complaints with DOB permit filings to identify which projects may be triggering violations
Interview DOB inspectors about whether the Hill Top Apartments development is driving ancillary code violations on neighboring buildings

themes_detail.label: Encampment complaints plateau after spike
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints spiked to 10 TWO WEEKS AGO (471% above 1.8 weekly average, z-score: 4.3), and while this is the oldest signal in the dataset, it remains a sustained high-severity issue warranting follow-up on whether conditions have worsened or merely become normalized.
evidence: 10 Encampment complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.8 weekly average (z-score: 4.3)
No recent Reddit discussions or community board agendas mention encampments, suggesting either resolution or normalization

Community Board budget requests include 'Allocate funds for outreach services to homebound older adults and for programs that allow the elder,' suggesting chronic homelessness/housing instability is a known ongoing problem
reporting_angles: Interview Park Maintenance and NYPD on current encampment status; determine whether the spike resolved or if complaints dropped because residents stopped reporting
Profile one or more individuals in encampments to understand barriers to housing in Morningside Heights and what services exist
